chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Abu

Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who went to his wife while he was fasting and she was fasting, so he said: If he coerced her, then upon him are two expiations; and if she consented, then upon him is an expiation and upon her is an expiation; and if he coerced her, then upon him is the striking of fifty lashes, being half the Hadd; and if she consented, he is struck with twenty-five lashes and she is struck with twenty-five lashes.
ai.seo_question: What are the different legal consequences for a husband and wife who break their Ramadan fast together, depending on whether one coerced the other?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential distinctions in expiation (kaffarah) and corporal punishment (hadd) for marital intercourse during Ramadan, emphasizing that coercion exempts the wife from expiation while imposing a reduced lash penalty on both parties. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of differentiating between voluntary transgression and forced compliance, ensuring justice in penalizing the guilty party while mitigating the penalty for the coerced. The ruling underscores the principle that the husband bears the primary responsibility for the act's initiation, yet both share liability if consent is mutual.
